issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a fully implemented Meal class (with name and ingredients fields and appropriate getters), but the template repository does not provide this: Meal.java is empty and instead the template contains an Order.java class with the same structure. This mismatch (missing/empty Meal class and presence of Order class) is structural and will confuse or block students because the exercise description, UML, and solution use Meal, not Order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the problem statement: provide a fully implemented Meal.java class (matching the UML and the solution) and remove or rename Order.java. Update any template code (e.g., Main) that references Order to use Meal. Ensure Meal.java contains the constructor and getters as described so students can implement SealSaloon against the correct type.

issues.description: The problem statement describes a Meal class (name and ingredients) that students are expected to use, but the template repository provides an Order class with the same structure. The solution repository uses Meal. This inconsistent naming (Meal vs Order) across artifacts creates a mapping confusion: students reading the problem will look for Meal but find Order in the template, which may lead to uncertainty about which class to modify or instantiate.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Rename the template's Order class to Meal (and its file to Meal.java), keeping the same fields and accessors, and update any references (e.g., Main) accordingly so the template matches the problem statement and the solution naming.
